2780234117.inscription_2: William (Billy) Ashley Sunday, famed evangelist, was born here on his grandfather Cory's farm on November 19, 1862. Here are buried 17 Cory family members, including Sunday's mother, Mary, his brother, Albert, and grandparents, Squire and Mary A. Cory.
2780234117.inscription_3: Sunday's father, a Union Army casualty, is buried in Missouri. Sunday attended a one-room school 1/2 mile west of this spot, and continued on at Nevada High School. He was a professional baseball player when he chose to enter the ministry.
2780234117.inscription_4: A dynamic, fiery orator, he drew record crowds in Iowa's towns and the nation's largest cities. Sunday died on November 6, 1935 and is buried in Chicago.

2798814395.inscription: From 1891 to 2001 a lumber yard was located on this site, Block 38 of Blair's Second Addition, 408 Duff Avenue. On June 25, 1896 H.L. Munn became the first Munn family member to become associated with the business.
2798814395.inscription_2: That tradition would continue well after the business was relocated when the lumber yard was destroyed by fire on August 2, 2001.
2798814395.inscription_3: Along with H.L. Munn, generations of Munns, including Alfred (Fred), Hiram, Alfred (Fritz), and Erik were involved with the business.
2798814395.inscription_4: In 2003, the City of Ames Electric Utility purchased the site from the Munn Family and developed the existing green space.
2798814395.name: H.L. Munn Memorial

2831763810.inscription: Durham Bandshell In 1928, Charles (Chuck) Durham moved with his parents, John and Monica (Monie) Durham, to a residence just north of Bandshell Park.
2831763810.inscription_2: John worked for the State Highway Commission and Chuck and a paper route that served the households surrounding Bandshell Park.
2831763810.inscription_3: Chuck stated on many occasions that his father's work ethic and his experience delivering newspapers gave him the fundamentals to run a business.
2831763810.inscription_4: Chuck went on to graduate from Ames High School in 1935 and then from Iowa State with two degrees in engineering. In 1940, Chuck moved to Omaha and joined the Henningson Engineering Company.
2831763810.inscription_5: On October 12, 1940, Chuck married the love of his life, Margre Henningson. Together they shared 59 years of marriage and were blessed with children and grandchildren.
2831763810.inscription_6: Chuck led Henningson Engineering Company, later called HDR, into an international giant of architecture, engineering, and construction. The contributions of the Durham's to Ames, Iowa, the Midwest and the world are too numerous to list.
2831763810.inscription_7: This plaque, from the Ames Foundation, recognizes the Durham Family's donation to the restoration of the Bandshell, completed in 2006.
2831763810.name: Durham Bandshell Memorial

2523376886.inscription: The Medicine Wheel is Sacred! The Great Spirit caused everything to be round: Sun, Sky, Moon, Earth.  It is the Circle of Life.
2523376886.inscription_2: Inside the Circle are: The Four Directions, The Four Winds, The Four Seasons.  This Medicine Wheel is in Honor of the First Nation People of the Great Plains.
2523376886.inscription_3: It is our hope that this park and this medicine wheel and this outdoor theater will become and remain as a sacred place.
